_comment: Per-work notes, keyed exactly as src/content/works.json keys its index. Written by /modernize-hopper, one work at a time, from named sources only. Every claim carries a source key that resolves in "sources" below; a note with no source is not a note. Nothing here is derived from a ledger row — the rows are on the sheets and the site shows them — and nothing is written from memory.

american landscape.note: Leaf 28’s row for 8 May 1925 is followed by a second: an impression handed to E. P. Jennings as his commission on the Metropolitan purchase, with a dash where the money would go. The Met’s impression is 25.31.4, dated 1920 as the leaf’s heading is, at a plate of 7 5/16 x 12 3/8 in. against the leaf’s 7 1/2" x 12 1/2".

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1920, Plate: 7 5/16 x 12 3/8 in. (18.5 x 31.4 cm), accession 25.31.4, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Book I leaf 28 heads the plate « American Landscape.  7 1/2" x 12 1/2"  1920 », records « Bought by Metropolitan Museum of Art - group price » at $10, and on the next line « this print was Commission to E. P. Jennings on Metrop. Mus. purchase », June 1925.

aux fortifications.note: Leaf 22 gives « size of plate 12"x15" », which rounds up both museums’ measurements — the Art Institute’s 11 13/16 × 14 15/16 in. and the Met’s 11 3/4 x 14 3/4. Both date it 1923, and Chicago calls it etching and drypoint where the leaf gives only the size. The Met’s impression is 25.31.5, from the lot the row of 8 May 1925 books at the group price of $10.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1923, Plate: 11 3/4 x 14 3/4 in. (29.9 x 37.5 cm), accession 25.31.5, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.
Book I leaf 22 heads the plate « Aux Fortifications  size of plate 12"x15" » and writes « Bought by Metrop. Museum - group price » at $10 on 8 May 1925.

blackwell s island.note: The Whitney's Blackwell's Island is a different canvas from this one: it is dated 1911 and its image measures 24 x 29 in., where both leaves here head the picture « Blackwell's Island - 35 x 60 » and Book II leaf 35 dates the painting « Nov. 20'', 28 ». The link and the year beside this entry are a title match and nothing stronger. Both ledgers carry this canvas and each sends the reader to the other: Book I leaf 57 writes « See Book II p. 35 », and Book II leaf 35 writes « See Book I p. 57 » and, in pencil at the edge, « This listed in Book I ». They give the same size and the same sale — 2500 less a third, 19 December 1929 — one as « 1666.67 » and the other as « 1666 2/3 », and they part over the buyer’s name, which Book I writes « Wm. Russell Allen » and then « Wm. C. Russell Allan » and Book II « Russel Allen ». On how it passed to Christopher Tunnard, Book I says a nephew acquired it and Book II « son-in-law or nephew ».

claims.says: The Whitney Museum of American Art holds a Blackwell's Island, oil on canvas, dated 1911, overall 24 3/8 × 29 5/16 in. (61.9 × 74.5 cm) and image 24 × 29 in. (61 × 73.7 cm), accession 70.1188, Josephine N. Hopper Bequest.

Book I leaf 57 heads « Blackwell's Island - 35 x 60 », books « Nov. 20, 28  Mr. Wm. Russell Allen of Boston - about Feb. or Mar.  2500 - 1/3 Com.  1666.67  Dec. 19, 29 », then « Wm. C. Russell Allan - Later acquired by nephew » and « See Book II p. 35.  Mr & Mrs. Christopher Tunnard, architect (city planning), 257 Rock Road, New Haven, Conn. »

Book II leaf 35 heads « Blackwell's Island  35 x 60 », says « Painted in N.Y. Studio. Nov. 20'', 28 » and « See Book I p. 57 », books « Bought by Russel Allen of Boston  1929.  2500 - 1/3 Com =  1666 2/3  Dec. 19, 1929 », and adds in pencil « Present owner Christopher Tunnard, architect » who got it because « Russel Allen gone for the abstract in Boston so got rid of this canvas to son-in-law or nephew », with « This listed in Book I » at the left edge.

bootleggers.note: The cross-reference is in her hand: Book I leaf 53 heads the canvas « Bootleggers  30 x 38  See Book II, p. 71 », and leaf 71 of Book II is that page, at the same size. Leaf 53 carries five exhibitions between 1925 and 1927 and a line naming Carl Hamilton and three canvases at 3000 in 1928; leaf 71 carries one sale, to the « Corrier Gallery, Manchester, N.H. » at 4000 less a third on 7 April 1956. Neither leaf says how the 1928 line and the 1956 sale stand to one another.

claims.says: Book I leaf 53 heads it « Bootleggers   30 x 38   See Book II, p. 71 », lists it invited or shown at the Rehn Gallery and the Brooklyn Museum in 1925, the Tri-National Ex. at Wildenstein's and the St. Botolph's Club in Boston in 1926 and the Rehn Gallery in 1927, and writes « Carl Hamilton of Cal. --- 1928. --- 3 canvases  Bootleggers, 11 A. M., Gloucester St.  3000 ».
Book II leaf 71 heads it « « Bootleggers »  30 x 38  1924 or 1925  Painted in Wash. Sq. studio » and books « Corrier Gallery, Manchester, N.H.  4000 - 1/3 =  2666 2/3,  Ap. 7, '56 ».

bull fight.note: The Art Institute dates it « c. 1917 », an approximation; leaf 43 heads the plate with a size, « 5" x 7" », and no year at all. Chicago’s plate measures 4 7/8 × 6 15/16 in., and the leaf’s earliest row is an acceptance by the Chicago Society of Etchers at the Art Institute, 7 February 1920.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Bull Fight, etching on white wove paper, dated c. 1917, Image/plate: 12.3 × 17.5 cm (4 7/8 × 6 15/16 in.); Sheet: 23.4 × 28.8 cm (9 1/4 × 11 3/8 in.), accession 1944.148, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 43 heads the plate « The Bull Fight  5" x 7" » and opens its table with « Feb. 7, 20  A  Chicago Society of Etchers, Art Inst. »

cat boat.note: The leaf heads it « The Cat Boat  8"x10"  1922 »; both museums date it 1922 and both measure the plate a shade under, at 7 13/16 x 9 13/16 and 7 7/8 × 9 7/8 in. Its row of 8 May 1925 writes the Metropolitan sale as « $18 group price » with $10 received — the list price and the lot price on one line — and the impression is 25.31.13.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1922, Plate: 7 13/16 x 9 13/16 in. (19.9 x 25 cm), accession 25.31.13, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Cat Boat, etching on off-white wove paper, dated 1922, Plate: 20 × 25 cm (7 7/8 × 9 7/8 in.); Sheet: 28 × 32.7 cm (11 1/16 × 12 7/8 in.), accession 1944.153, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.
Book I leaf 10 heads the plate « The Cat Boat  8"x10"  1922 » and writes « Bought by Metrop. Museum - $18 group price », $10 received 8 May 1925.

compartment c.note: The Art Institute bought it in 1938 and gave it back four years later: leaf 25 books the purchase at 1000 less a third on 14 May 1938 and then « Returned by Art Inst. " C in part payment for Night Hawks. May 19, 42 », which is the 1000 leaf 95 sets against a 3000 canvas. It sold again in June 1943, to Thos. J. Watson through the Grand Central Galleries, at 900 — a hundred less than the museum had paid — and the leaf adds that the Art Institute had changed the original frame.

claims.says: Book II leaf 25 heads it « Compartment C  Car 293.  18"x20"  Mar. 30, '38 », books « Art Institute, Chicago.  1000 - 1/3 =  666 2/3  May 14, 1938 », then the return of 19 May 1942, then « Thos. J. Watson of International Machine Co. - thru Grand Central Galleries from Rehn Gal. » at « 900 - 1/3 = 600. Jun 19, 43 », with « ( Frame changed again. Art Inst. frame no good. They had changed original frame. »
Book II leaf 95 books the Night Hawks sale of 13 May 1942 as « 3000 + return of Compartment C. 1000 », marginally « in exchange as part payment. »
The Art Institute of Chicago gives Nighthawks the provenance « consigned to Frank Rehn Galleries, 1942; sold to the Art Institute of Chicago, 1942 », accession 1942.51.

corner.note: Leaf 44 gives « A Corner  3 1/4 x 4 » and the Art Institute’s plate is 3 1/4 × 3 15/16 in. — the height exact, the width rounded up by a sixteenth. Chicago dates it 1919; the leaf gives no year, and its first row is the Chicago Society of Etchers at the Art Institute, 7 February 1920, with $10 received on 8 April 1925.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as A Corner, etching on ivory wove paper, dated 1919, Plate: 8.2 × 10 cm (3 1/4 × 3 15/16 in.); Sheet: 19.1 × 20.4 cm (7 9/16 × 8 1/16 in.), accession 1944.141, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 44 heads the plate « A Corner  3 1/4 x 4 » and its first row reads « Feb. 7, 20  A  Chicago Soc. of Etchers, Art Inst. » with $10 received 8 April 1925.

corner saloon.note: Leaf 69 is about Rail Road Train, Squam Light and El Station, and twice carries an erased pencil line belonging to none of them — « Corner Saloon 1913  See p. 87 » — once under the heading and once inside the empty drawing box ruled for Squam Light. Page 87 is that leaf, which dates the picture 1913 and records the Museum of Modern Art buying it out of the Rehn show of early work in January 1941, part in cash and part in two watercolours the museum already had from Mrs. John D. Rockefeller, Jr.

claims.says: Book II leaf 69 carries « Corner Saloon -1913-  p. 87  Bk. II. » under its heading and « Corner Saloon 1913  See p. 87. » inside the empty drawing box beside Squam Light, both in erased pencil that can still be read.

Book II leaf 87 heads « Corner Saloon  24 x 29 », says « Painted 1913. Taken to Rehn Gallery Jan. 1941 for show of Early work », and records it « Bought out of Hopper show of Early work, Jan. 1941 - by Museum of Modern Art, with 2 old water colors given some years before by Mrs. John D. Rockefeller, Jr. », at « Amt. rec'd 800 - 1/3 =  533 1/3  Ap. 19, 41 ».

cow and rocks.note: Leaf 36 writes « 7" x 8" plate size », saying what the figures measure, against the Art Institute’s 6 15/16 × 7 7/8 in. Chicago dates it 1918, two years before the leaf’s earliest row — a refusal by the Chicago Society of Etchers on 7 February 1920 — and the leaf gives no year of its own.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as Cow and Rocks, etching on ivory wove paper, dated 1918, Image/plate: 17.5 × 20 cm (6 15/16 × 7 7/8 in.); Sheet: 27.2 × 28.3 cm (10 3/4 × 11 3/16 in.), accession 1944.149, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 36 heads the plate « Cow & Rocks  7" x 8" plate size. » and opens its table with « Feb. 7, 20  R  Chicago Society of Etchers, Art Inst. »

east side interior.note: Leaf 8 books the Chicago Society of Etchers’ award of 23 February 1923 as « Logan Prize - not purchase », $25, and the line beneath it records two prints sold through the Society for $28.80. The Art Institute’s impression is accession 1923.305, credited to the Mr. and Mrs. Frank G. Logan Purchase Prize Fund and taken in that year; which of those two lines it came in on is not settled by either record. The Met’s impression is 25.31.1, the first number of the 1925 lot the leaf books at $10 on 8 May.

Book I leaf 8 writes « Feb. 23, 23  A  Chicago Soc. of Etchers.  Logan Prize - not purchase » at $25, and on the next line « Sale = $18 - Com. Shicago Soc. », 2 prints, $28.80.

evening wind.note: The Art Institute measures its impression’s plate at 7 × 8 3/8 in., which is leaf 2’s heading to the sixteenth; the Met’s own impression comes out a little smaller, at 6 15/16 x 8 1/4. Jennings, $10 received on 8 May — is the artist’s side of accession 25.31.7, one of fifteen Hopper etchings the museum took in a single 1925 lot.

Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.
Book I leaf 2 heads the plate « Evening Wind  7 x 8 3/8" » and records « Bought by Metropolitan Museum - thru E. Jennings » at $10, received 8 May 1925.

Book I leaf 34 heads the plate « Girl on a Bridge  7"x9"  1923 ».

henry ford.note: Leaf 39 gives the plate as « 12" x 15" » and the Art Institute measures its impression at 11 13/16 × 14 7/8 in. Chicago dates it 1923; the leaf carries no year and only three rows, the first a refusal by the Brooklyn Society of Etchers on 5 October 1925.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Henry Ford, etching on ivory wove paper, dated 1923, Image/plate: 30 × 37.7 cm (11 13/16 × 14 7/8 in.); Sheet: 35.1 × 43.8 cm (13 7/8 × 17 1/4 in.), accession 1944.161, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 39 heads the plate « The Henry Ford  12" x 15" » and opens with « Oct. 5, 25  R  Bklyn. Soc. Etchers, Bklyn. Mus. »

hills south truro.note: Cleveland dates the canvas 1930 and accessioned it in 1931 — its number, 1931.2647, carries the year — which is the sale Book I leaf 59 writes as « Cleveland Museum. Nov. 9, 31 » at 2000 less a third. The ledger and the museum are independent records of one transaction, and they agree.

claims.says: Cleveland Museum of Art holds it, oil on canvas, dated 1930, accession 1931.2647, Hinman B. Hurlbut Collection.
Book I leaf 59 records the sale to the Cleveland Museum, 9 November 1931, at 2000 less one third.

house by a river.note: Leaf 18 heads the plate « House by a River  7"x8"  1920 » and the Art Institute dates its impression 1919. The leaf’s earliest row is the Touchstone Galleries, 17 October 1920, which is consistent with either year and settles neither.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as House by a River, etching on off-white wove paper, dated 1919, Image/plate: 17.5 × 20.1 cm (6 15/16 × 7 15/16 in.); Sheet: 25.3 × 28.6 cm (10 × 11 5/16 in.), accession 1944.152, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 18 heads the plate « House by a River  7"x8"  1920 » and opens its table with « Oct. 17, 20  A  Touchstone Galleries ».

house tops.note: Both museums put the plate at 14.8 × 19.9 cm and render that in inches differently — 5 13/16 x 7 13/16 at the Met, 5 7/8 × 7 7/8 in Chicago — where leaf 32 gives a flat « 6"x8" ». Its Metropolitan row of 8 May 1925 is five months before the Brooklyn Museum bought an impression out of the Society of Etchers show at $15 less 15%, and the Met’s is 25.31.10.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1921, Plate: 5 13/16 x 7 13/16 in. (14.8 x 19.9 cm), accession 25.31.10, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Book I leaf 32 heads the plate « House Tops.  6"x8" », writes « Bought by Metropolitan Museum - group price » at $10 on 8 May 1925, and on 5 October 1925 « $15 - 15% bought by Mus. » at the Brooklyn Museum, $12.75 received 14 January 1926.

les deux pigeons.note: The Met catalogues the French title the leaf writes and the Art Institute an English The Two Pigeons; the site links all three through declared aliases. claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1920, Plate: 8 3/8 x 9 7/8 in. (21.2 x 25.1 cm), accession 25.31.6, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Two Pigeons, etching on off-white wove paper, dated 1920, Image/plate: 21.3 × 25 cm (8 7/16 × 9 7/8 in.); Sheet: 29 × 32.8 cm (11 7/16 × 12 15/16 in.), accession 1944.155, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.
Book I leaf 40 heads the plate « Les Deux Pigeon  8 1/2" x 10" » and writes « Bought by Metropolitan Museum of Art - group price » at $10, received 8 May 1925.

locomotive.note: Leaf 14 heads the plate « The Locomotive  1922 »; the Art Institute and Cleveland both date it 1923. claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Locomotive, etching and drypoint on white wove paper, dated 1923, Plate: 20.1 × 25.2 cm (7 15/16 × 9 15/16 in.); Sheet: 28.6 × 33.6 cm (11 5/16 × 13 1/4 in.), accession 1944.146, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
The Cleveland Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1923, accession 1958.382, Gift of William Ellery Greene for the Lucy S. Greene Collection.
Book I leaf 14 heads the plate « The Locomotive  1922 » and opens its table with « Nov. 1, 23  A  N. A. D. »

lonely house.note: Leaf 26 heads the plate « The Lonely House.  8"x10"  1922 »; the Met and the Art Institute both date it 1923. The leaf’s earliest row is a refusal by the Brooklyn Society of Etchers on 24 October 1922, a date the museums’ year does not accommodate, and the disagreement stands. The same leaf writes the Metropolitan purchase « May 5, 25 » against the « May 8 » of its own received column.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1923, Plate: 7 13/16 x 9 13/16 in. (19.9 x 25 cm), accession 25.31.12, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Lonely House, etching and drypoint on white wove paper, dated 1923, Plate: 19.9 × 25 cm (7 7/8 × 9 7/8 in.); Sheet: 29 × 33.8 cm (11 7/16 × 13 5/16 in.), accession 1944.145, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.

Book I leaf 26 heads the plate « The Lonely House.  8"x10"  1922 », opens with « Oct. 24, 22  R  Bklyn. Soc. of Etchers », and dates the Metropolitan purchase « May 5, 25 » with « May 8, 25 » in the received column.

monhegan boat.note: The leaf gives the plate as « 7"x9" » and no year; Chicago dates its impression 1918 and measures 6 15/16 × 8 7/8 in. Leaf 16’s first sale is to the State Library, Los Angeles, at $18, $16.20 received on 17 May 1920, and its twelve rows stop in April 1926 — eighteen years before the Print and Drawing Club gave the Art Institute this impression.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as The Monhegan Boat, etching on white wove paper, dated 1918, Image/plate: 17.5 × 22.5 cm (6 15/16 × 8 7/8 in.); Sheet: 24.2 × 29.8 cm (9 9/16 × 11 3/4 in.), accession 1944.151, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.

Book I leaf 16 heads the plate « The Monhegan Boat  7"x9" », records a sale to the State Library, Los Angeles at $18 with $16.20 received on 17 May 1920, and ends with the St. Botolph’s Club show of 12 April 1926.

Both date it 1918 and put the plate near 7 3/8 x 7 13/16 in. against the leaf’s 7 1/2" x 8". The Met’s impression is 25.31.11, from the 8 May 1925 lot the leaf books at $10.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1918, Plate: 7 3/8 x 7 13/16 in. (18.7 x 19.9 cm), accession 25.31.11, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

Book I leaf 30 heads the plate « Night in the L Train  7 1/2" x 8". » and writes « Bought by Metropolitan Mus. - group price » at $10 on 8 May 1925.

night shadows.note: Leaf 6 heads the plate « Night Shadows  7"x8 3/8"  1921 » and all three museums that hold an impression date it 1921. The Met’s is 25.31.2, from the lot the leaf books at $10 on 8 May 1925; Chicago’s came from the Print and Drawing Club in 1944 and Cleveland’s as a gift from Mrs. Malcolm L. McBride in 1959, both long after the leaf’s last row.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1921, Plate: 6 7/8 x 8 3/16 in. (17.4 x 20.8 cm), accession 25.31.2, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as Night Shadows, etching on white wove paper, dated 1921, Plate: 17.5 × 21 cm (6 15/16 × 8 5/16 in.); Sheet: 25.6 × 28 cm (10 1/8 × 11 1/16 in.), accession 1944.156, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
The Cleveland Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1921, accession 1959.298, Gift of Mrs. Malcolm L. McBride.
Book I leaf 6 heads the plate « Night Shadows  7"x8 3/8"  1921 », records « Bought by Metropolitan Mus. (Wm. Ivans) group price » at $10 on 8 May 1925, and ends in November 1927.

nighthawks.note: The Art Institute measures the canvas at 33 1/8 x 60 in. against leaf 95’s « 33 x 60 », dates it 1942, and gives its provenance as consigned to Rehn and sold to the museum that year — which is the row the leaf writes « May 13, 42 » at 3000 plus the return of Compartment C at 1000, less a third. Leaf 25 is the other end of that exchange: the Art Institute had bought Compartment C in 1938 and hands it back six days after this sale. The prize entered on the leaf for 27 October 1942 falls two days before the Fifty-third Annual opened in Chicago, which the museum’s exhibition history lists this picture in.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds it, oil on canvas, 84.1 × 152.4 cm (33 1/8 × 60 in.), dated 1942, accession 1942.51, Friends of American Art Collection. Provenance: « The artist, New York; consigned to Frank Rehn Galleries, 1942; sold to the Art Institute of Chicago, 1942. » Its exhibition history opens with the Art Institute’s Fifty-third Annual Exhibition of American Paintings and Sculpture, 29 October to 10 December 1942, cat. 132.

Book II leaf 95 heads it « Night Hawks  33 x 60 », dates it « Finished Jan 21, 1942 », and books « May 13, 42  Chicago Art Institute - 3000 + return of Compartment C. 1000 » at « - Com. 1/3 = 2000 », then « Oct. 27, 42 » the « Ada S. Garret Prize » of $750.
Book II leaf 25 records the Art Institute of Chicago buying Compartment C on 14 May 1938 and « Returned by Art Inst. " C in part payment for Night Hawks. May 19, 42. »

sailing.note: Both ledgers call this the first canvas he sold, out of the Armory Show of 1913, which is the sale the Whitney’s own chronology puts in that year. They do not agree on the money: Book I leaf 52 writes « Sold at International Armory Show 1913 --- $225 » and then « Sold to Mr. Vietor, 25" & Mad. Ave.  250 - 10% », where Book II leaf 68 has « ± $250 ». They part again over its reappearance — Book I’s margin says it turned up in the fall of 1949 and was bought in Pittsburg for $1,000, Book II that it came to the Rehn Gallery about 1951 and was resold for $1200 to Mrs. Becky Beal of Pittsburg.

claims.says: Hopper sold his first canvas at the Armory Show in 1913.

Book I leaf 52 heads « Sailing » and writes « Sold at International Armory Show 1913 --- $225.   1913 », « Sold to Mr. Vietor, 25" & Mad. Ave.  250 - 10% » with « Sold by Arthur B. Davies » struck, and in the margin « turned up fall 1949  Sold to Mr. [illegible]  Bought in Pittsburg $1,000. »

Book II leaf 68 heads « Sailing  1913 or before  24 x 29 » under « Early Oils » and writes « Sold out of famous Armory Show - 1913.  ± $250. », that it was the first canvas of E.H. sold, and « Turned up + brought to Rehn Gal. ± 1951 + resold for $1200. for owner - Bqt. by [Mrs.] Becky Beal, Pittsburg ».

summer twilight.note: Leaf 42 gives « 8 1/2" x 10" » and the Art Institute measures 8 7/16 × 9 15/16 in., dating it 1920 where the leaf gives no year. The leaf’s second row is not a sale: Weyhe presented an impression to « Meyer Graefe », with a dash in the amount column.

claims.says: The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as Summer Twilight, etching on off-white wove paper, dated 1920, Image/plate: 21.3 × 25.1 cm (8 7/16 × 9 15/16 in.); Sheet: 28.8 × 32.4 cm (11 3/8 × 12 13/16 in.), accession 1944.143, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Book I leaf 42 heads the plate « Summer Twilight  8 1/2" x 10" » and records « Weyhe presented to Meyer Graefe » with a dash where the amount would stand.

tables for ladies.note: The Met gives the canvas as 48 1/4 by 60 3/8 inches, which is the « 4 x 5 ft. » of Book I leaf 59 to within an inch — the leaf's rounding, not a different picture. It was bought with the George A. Hearn Fund in 1931; the leaf puts the cheque at 3 June 1931, on a price of 4500 less a third.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds it, oil on canvas, 48 1/4 x 60 3/8 in., dated 1930, acquired 1931 through the George A. Hearn Fund.
Book I leaf 59 gives the size as 4 x 5 ft. and the sale to the Metropolitan at 4500 less a third, received 3 June 1931.

train and bathers.note: The leaf’s « 8 1/2" x 10" » rounds up a plate the Met puts at 8 5/16 x 9 13/16 in. and Chicago at 8 3/8 × 9 7/8; both date it 1920 and the leaf gives no year. Its row of 8 May 1925 is the Metropolitan’s group purchase at $10, and the impression is 25.31.9.

claims.says: The Metropolitan Museum of Art holds an impression, etching, dated 1920, Plate: 8 5/16 x 9 13/16 in. (21.1 x 25 cm), accession 25.31.9, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.

The Art Institute of Chicago holds an impression as Train and Bathers, etching on white wove paper, dated 1920, Image/plate: 21.2 × 25 cm (8 3/8 × 9 7/8 in.); Sheet: 30.5 × 33.7 cm (12 1/16 × 13 5/16 in.), accession 1944.142, Gift of the Print and Drawing Club.
Accession lot 25.31 is fifteen Edward Hopper etchings, 25.31.1 to 25.31.15, all credited Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925.
Book I leaf 38 heads the plate « Train & Bathers  8 1/2" x 10" » and writes « Bought by Metropolitan Museum - (group price) » at $10, received 8 May 1925.
